weeks.title: Build a sentence
weeks.spanish: Identifica sujeto y verbo. Con he/she/it o un sujeto singular, agrega -s: the coordinator checks; my job needs it. Con I/you/we/they usa verbo base. Usa need to + verbo para una acción necesaria.

weeks.title: Now or usually?
weeks.spanish: Usa presente simple para hábitos; am/is/are + -ing para acciones en curso.

weeks.title: Tell the story
weeks.spanish: Usa pasado simple para acciones terminadas. Después de did usa verbo base; send cambia a sent. Usa the para algo identificado. Las frases son work on y wait for.

weeks.title: Connect your ideas
weeks.spanish: Relaciona ideas: because da una razón, so da un resultado y but introduce contraste.

weeks.title: Share an update
weeks.spanish: Da un avance, un bloqueo y un siguiente paso. Usa need to + verbo.

weeks.title: Plan what comes next
weeks.spanish: Will sirve para decisiones o predicciones; going to para planes. Present continuous también expresa acuerdos.

weeks.title: Make meetings useful
weeks.spanish: Después de do, does y did usa el verbo base. Pide aclaración con preguntas concretas.

weeks.title: Work through dependencies
weeks.spanish: Nombra la dependencia, explica su impacto y pide una acción con fecha.

weeks.title: Lead a conversation
weeks.spanish: Usa peticiones claras y corteses. Distingue un riesgo posible de un problema actual.

weeks.title: Negotiate a deadline
weeks.spanish: Explica la restricción y ofrece una alternativa viable. If + presente, will + verbo.

weeks.title: Tell your professional story
weeks.spanish: Organiza una respuesta con situación, acción y resultado. Usa ejemplos ficticios.

weeks.title: Bring it all together
weeks.spanish: Une pasado, presente y futuro. Resume lo esencial y confirma el siguiente paso.

rows: Introduce your tech lead role
What do you do on Project Orion? I coordinate the software team.
The speaker coordinates a software team.
I ___ the software team.
coordinate
She coordinate the software team.
She coordinates the software team.
With I, use coordinate. With she, he, or it, add -s: she coordinates. A tech lead helps a software team plan and make technical decisions.
Name a technical responsibility
Who checks the test results? The tech lead checks them every Friday.
The tech lead checks the results each Friday.
The tech lead ___ the results.
checks
He need a clear plan.
He needs a clear plan.
The tech lead is one person, so use checks. Use needs with he; I, you, we, and they use the base form.
Ask about an engineering role
Does the engineer join the team meeting? Yes, she joins every Monday.
The engineer joins a regular team meeting.
___ the engineer join meetings?
Does
Does she joins meetings?
Does she join meetings?
After does, use the base verb join. Join a meeting means take part in it.
Ask for everyday help
What do you need to make dinner? We need to buy rice first.
They need rice before making dinner.
We need ___ buy rice.
to
We need buy rice.
We need to buy rice.
Use need to + base verb for a necessary action. Buy rice is a natural everyday phrase.
Introduce a new neighbor
Are you our new neighbor? Yes, I am. I live here with my sister.
The new neighbor lives with a sister.
I ___ your new neighbor.
am
I is your new neighbor.
I am your new neighbor.
Use am with I, is with he or she, and are with we or they. Neighbor is the American spelling.
Describe a testing routine
How often do you run the tests? I run them every morning before our team meeting.
The speaker runs the tests every morning.
I usually ___ the tests before the meeting.
run
She run the tests every day.
She runs the tests every day.
Every morning describes a routine, so use present simple. Run tests means execute checks on the software.
Say what you are building
What are you working on this week? I am building an API that lets our app share data.
The API lets the app share data.
I am ___ an API.
building
I building an API.
I am building an API.
Use am + -ing for work in progress. An API lets software exchange information; learn the phrase building an API in context.
Contrast routine and incident work
Do you usually review code in the morning? Yes, but today I am checking an error in the app.
Today the speaker is checking an app error.
Today she ___ checking an error.
is
She check an error right now.
She is checking an error right now.
Use present simple for a routine and is + -ing for a temporary action happening now. Review code means examine changes to the software.
Talk about a current activity
Is your brother cooking dinner? Not yet. He is buying vegetables at the store.
The brother is buying vegetables now.
He is ___ vegetables.
buying
He is buy vegetables.
He is buying vegetables.
After is in the continuous, use the -ing form. At the store and buying vegetables are everyday American expressions.
Explain a choice at home
What does your family need today? It needs a grocery list, and we are writing one together.
The family is writing a grocery list.
The family ___ a grocery list.
needs
The family need to deciding.
The family needs to decide.
A singular subject takes needs. After needs to, use decide, not deciding. A grocery list helps you plan what to buy.
Report a bug fix
What did you finish yesterday? I fixed the sign-in bug before lunch and sent the test results.
The speaker fixed the bug before lunch.
Yesterday I ___ the test results.
sent
Yesterday I fix the bug.
Yesterday I fixed the bug.
Use past simple for completed work: fix becomes fixed and send becomes sent. A bug is a defect in software, such as a sign-in failure.
Ask about an API decision
Did they approve the API design? No, they asked for a clearer example of the response.
The API design was not approved.
Did they ___ the API design?
approve
Did they approved the API design?
Did they approve the API design?
After did, use the base verb approve. An API response is the information the API sends back.
Find a status report
Where is the status report we discussed? It is in the shared folder, with the dates and open issues.
The status report is in a shared folder.
Please open ___ status report we discussed.
the
Please open status report we discussed.
Please open the status report we discussed.
Use the for a specific document both speakers know. A status report is a structured record of progress, dates, and issues; a weekly update can be a brief spoken summary.
Describe a personal project
What are you working on at home? I am working on a photo album, but I am waiting for more pictures.
The speaker is waiting for more pictures.
I am working ___ a photo album.
on
I am working in a photo album.
I am working on a photo album.
Use work on for a task or project and wait for for something you need. In American English, pictures and photos are both common.
Tell a weekend story
How was your trip to the park? We found a quiet spot, had lunch, and walked around the lake.
They had lunch at a quiet spot.
We ___ a quiet spot at the park.
found
We find a quiet spot yesterday.
We found a quiet spot yesterday.
Find becomes found in the past. Use a sequence of past actions to tell a short story.
Explain a deployment delay
Why is the deployment delayed? One test failed, so we are fixing it before we deploy the app.
A failed test caused the deployment delay.
The test failed, ___ we paused the deployment.
so
The deployment is delayed because of one test failed.
The deployment is delayed because one test failed.
Because introduces a clause; because of needs a noun phrase. Deploy the app means put a version into its target environment; release means make a change available to users.
Contrast code and documentation
Is the service ready? The code is ready, but the API documentation still needs an example.
The API documentation still needs an example.
The code is ready, ___ the documentation is not.
but
Although the code is ready, but we need documentation.
Although the code is ready, we need documentation.
Use although with a clause without adding but to the same construction. A service can have working code and still need clear documentation.
Structure a weekly update
How should I give my weekly update? First, say what you finished. Next, name any blockers. Finally, explain your next step.
Completed work comes first in the weekly update.
___, say what you finished; next, name any blockers.
First
First name the blockers, finally give the next step, next explain the work.
First explain the work, next name the blockers, finally give the next step.
First, next, and finally order a spoken update. A weekly update summarizes the week's work; a status report is usually a more structured written record.
Ask someone to repeat a plan
Could you repeat that? Should we meet for coffee today or tomorrow? Tomorrow, please.
They plan to meet for coffee tomorrow.
Could you ___ that, please?
repeat
Could you to repeat that?
Could you repeat that?
After could, use a base verb without to. Repeat that is a natural way to ask someone to say something again.
Clarify an invitation
Let me clarify. Dinner is at my place on Saturday, not at the restaurant.
Dinner is at the speaker's home on Saturday.
What I ___ is that dinner is at my place.
mean
Let me to clarify the plan.
Let me clarify the plan.
Use let me + base verb. My place is an informal American way to say my home. What I mean is helps you clarify a message.
Give a weekly engineering update
What is your weekly update? We finished the API tests yesterday. Today we are checking the integration, and tomorrow we will share the results.
The team is checking the integration today.
Today we are ___ the integration.
checking
We finished yesterday and today we checks the integration.
We finished yesterday and today we are checking the integration.
Change tense with the time: finished yesterday, are checking today, will share tomorrow. A weekly update highlights progress and next steps; it is not necessarily a formal status report.
Describe an actual blocker
What is blocking testing? We cannot access the test environment because our account has no permission yet.
Missing access is preventing testing now.
We cannot start ___ without access.
testing
We cannot start to testing.
We cannot start testing.
Start can take testing or to test, but not to testing. A blocker prevents progress now. An issue is a current problem that may or may not block work; a risk is a possible future problem.
Explain an integration dependency
What does the integration depend on? It depends on the API contract, which the other team will confirm on Thursday.
The integration depends on the API contract.
The integration depends ___ the API contract.
on
The integration depends of the API contract.
The integration depends on the API contract.
Use depend on. An API contract describes what a request and response must contain. A dependency is something another step needs; it is not automatically a blocker.
Plan a family errand
What happens next? We need to pick up the groceries before we can make dinner.
Picking up groceries comes before dinner.
We need to ___ up the groceries.
pick
We need to picking up the groceries.
We need to pick up the groceries.
Need to takes a base verb. Pick up the groceries means collect the food you bought. Before connects the earlier action to the later one.
Handle a household problem
Are you still working on the broken bike? Yes, I am working on fixing it before Friday.
The speaker plans to fix the bike before Friday.
I am working on ___ the bike.
fixing
I am working on fix the bike.
I am working on fixing the bike.
After the preposition on, use a noun or an -ing form: working on fixing. A broken bike is a real current problem, not a future possibility.
Plan a small service change
What are you going to test next week? We are going to test two microservices together before changing the app.
The team will test two microservices together.
We are going ___ test the two services.
to
We going to test the services next week.
We are going to test the services next week.
Going to needs be: we are going to test. Microservices are small services with separate responsibilities; here the task is to check how two services work together.
Offer help during an incident
Who can check the logs while we restore the service? I will check them. Please keep the incident channel updated.
The speaker volunteers to check the logs.
I ___ check the logs.
will
I will to check the logs.
I will check the logs.
Will takes a base verb without to and can express a decision made now. Logs record events; an incident is a disruption that needs a coordinated response.
Confirm a deployment review
When are you meeting the architect? We are meeting her at ten tomorrow to review the deployment plan. It is on the calendar.
The deployment review is scheduled for ten tomorrow.
We ___ meeting the architect tomorrow.
are
We meeting her at ten tomorrow.
We are meeting her at ten tomorrow.
Present continuous can express an arranged future event. An architect helps the team reason about system structure and trade-offs.
Estimate time for a personal plan
When can you finish the photo album? I can finish it by Friday, but printing the pictures will take another day.
The album can be finished before the pictures are printed.
Printing will ___ another day.
take
Printing will takes another day.
Printing will take another day.
After will, use the base verb take. By Friday gives a deadline; another day means one additional day.
Make a conditional weekend plan
Will we go hiking on Saturday? If the weather is clear, we will go. Otherwise, we will stay home.
The hike depends on clear weather.
If the weather ___ clear, we will go.
is
If the weather will be clear, we will go.
If the weather is clear, we will go.
Use present simple after if and will in the result clause for a real future possibility. Otherwise introduces the alternative plan.
Open an architecture discussion
What should we cover first? Let's confirm the problem we need to solve. Then we can compare keeping one service with splitting it into two.
The discussion starts by clarifying the problem.
Let us ___ the problem first.
confirm
Let us to confirm the problem.
Let us confirm the problem.
Let us takes a base verb; let's is the common conversational form. Start an architecture discussion with the problem before comparing system designs.
Ask about API ownership
Who owns the API response format? The platform team owns it, and the architect will review the proposed change at two.
The platform team owns the response format.
When ___ the review start?
does
When does the review starts?
When does the review start?
Use does + subject + base verb in a present-simple question. Owns means is responsible for here; a response format defines how the API returns data.
Clarify a service change
I am not sure I understood. Are you asking us to change the API response or just its documentation? Just the documentation; the response stays the same.
Only the API documentation should change.
I am not sure I ___.
understood
I am not sure I understanded.
I am not sure I understood.
The past form of understand is understood. Offer two specific interpretations to avoid changing an API when only documentation needs work.
Interrupt to check rollback ownership
Sorry to jump in. Before we deploy, could we confirm who will roll back the change if the error rate goes up?
The speaker wants to confirm who will handle a rollback.
Sorry ___ jump in.
to
Sorry for jump in.
Sorry to jump in.
Sorry to jump in is a polite interruption. Roll back a change means return to the previous version; confirm the owner before deployment.
Agree on a shared weekend plan
What did we agree on? We agreed to meet at the park on Wednesday and bring lunch to share.
They agreed to meet at the park on Wednesday.
We agreed ___ meet at the park.
to
We agreed meet at the park.
We agreed to meet at the park.
Agree to + verb describes a decision to act. In conversation, What did we agree on? naturally asks about a shared plan.
Request an integration input
What do you need from us? We need the sample API response by noon so that we can finish the integration test today.
The sample response is needed by noon.
We need the response ___ noon.
by
We need the response until noon.
We need the response by noon.
By sets a deadline; until means an activity continues up to a time. A sample response gives the integration test realistic data without using production information.
Explain a dependency's impact
What happens if the API contract changes late? We will need two more days to update the integration tests before deployment.
A late contract change adds two days of test work.
A late change will ___ testing.
delay
A late change will delays testing.
A late change will delay testing.
Use will + base verb for a possible impact. State how much extra work a dependency change creates instead of calling every dependency a blocker.
Escalate a missing decision
Why are you escalating the access issue? We requested test-environment access on Monday and still have no decision. Testing is scheduled to start tomorrow.
Missing access threatens tomorrow's testing.
We asked ___ access on Monday.
for
We asked access on Monday.
We asked for access on Monday.
Ask for a thing; ask someone a question. Escalate an issue with request history, impact, and the decision needed, rather than blaming another team.
Prioritize by user impact
Which issue should we fix first? Fix the sign-in failure because users cannot access the app. The optional dashboard chart can wait.
The sign-in failure has higher priority.
The chart can ___ until tomorrow.
wait
The chart can waits until tomorrow.
The chart can wait until tomorrow.
After can, use a base verb. An issue is a current problem; this issue is also a blocker because it prevents users from signing in.
Compare everyday options
Should we take the bus or drive? The bus costs less; however, driving is faster. We need to choose before six.
The bus is cheaper, but driving is faster.
The bus costs less; ___, driving is faster.
however
The bus is cheaper; however, driving are faster.
The bus is cheaper; however, driving is faster.
Use a semicolon or a new sentence before however and a comma after it. Compare a benefit and a drawback when choosing an everyday option.
Delegate a technical review
Could you review the API change by Thursday and flag any compatibility issues? Yes, I will send comments before lunch.
The reviewer will check for compatibility issues.
Could you ___ the API change?
review
Could you reviews the API change?
Could you review the API change?
After could, use review. A clear tech lead request names the change, deadline, and concern. Flag an issue means point it out; compatibility asks whether existing clients still work.
Improve an engineering status report
What should I change in the status report? Keep the progress summary, but add an owner and a target date for each open issue. Mention possible delays as risks.
Open issues need an owner and a target date.
Each issue ___ an owner and a target date.
needs
Each issue need an owner.
Each issue needs an owner.
Each issue is singular, so use needs. A status report is a structured record. An engineering manager uses it to make ownership and dates clear; possible future delays are risks, not confirmed issues.
Distinguish a risk from an issue
Is the service slowdown confirmed? No. Traffic might increase next week, so there is a risk of slower responses. The service is working normally today.
Slower responses are a possible future risk.
The service ___ slow down next week.
might
The service might slows down.
The service might slow down.
After might, use a base verb. A risk may happen in the future; an issue exists now. A blocker prevents progress. Do not report a possible slowdown as an ongoing incident.
Reduce deployment risk
How can we reduce the deployment risk? Let's deploy to a small test group first, monitor the error rate, and keep a rollback plan ready.
The team proposes a limited deployment with monitoring.
Let us ___ the error rate.
monitor
Let us to monitor the error rate.
Let us monitor the error rate.
Use let us + base verb. Reduce risk by limiting exposure and checking results. A rollback plan describes how to return to the previous version if needed.
Balance two personal needs
Why not invite everyone tonight? I would like to see our friends. On the other hand, we need a quiet evening before tomorrow's trip.
The speakers are balancing friends and rest.
We want company. ___, we need rest.
On the other hand
We wants company but needs rest.
We want company, but we need rest.
Use want and need with we. On the other hand introduces a competing consideration, not just one more reason for the same choice.
Negotiate time for testing
Can you deploy tomorrow? We can finish the code tomorrow, but we need two more days for integration tests. Could we deploy on Friday instead?
Integration tests need two additional days.
We need two more days ___ integration tests.
for
We need two more days to integration tests.
We need two more days for integration tests.
Use for + noun phrase, or to + base verb. Distinguish code complete from tested and ready to deploy; offer a specific alternative date.
Negotiate a smaller scope
Is Friday still possible? Yes, if we leave out the optional export feature. We can deliver the core API on Friday and add exports in the next release.
Friday is possible with a smaller scope.
If we reduce the scope, we can ___ on Friday.
deliver
If we reduces the scope, we can deliver.
If we reduce the scope, we can deliver.
Use reduce with we and a base verb after can. Scope is the work included in a delivery; negotiate what can wait without hiding the trade-off.
Disagree respectfully about a deadline
Do you agree with the proposed date? I see the benefit, but I am concerned about the testing time. Could we keep one extra day to check the integration?
The speaker wants one extra day for integration testing.
I am concerned ___ the testing time.
about
I am concern about the testing time.
I am concerned about the testing time.
Use be concerned about + noun phrase. Acknowledge the benefit, name the concern, and ask for a concrete adjustment rather than agreeing to an unsafe deadline.
Confirm a delivery agreement
What is the final agreement? We will deliver the core API on Friday. The optional export feature will follow next Tuesday, and the tech lead will confirm the owners today.
The core API is due Friday and exports next Tuesday.
We will ___ the core API on Friday.
deliver
We will delivers the core API on Friday.
We will deliver the core API on Friday.
Will takes a base verb. Confirm scope, dates, and owners so that a technical decision becomes a clear delivery agreement.
Explain a missed personal deadline
Why did you miss the registration date? I misunderstood the deadline. I called the community center, and they helped me find another class.
The speaker found another class after missing registration.
I ___ the deadline.
misunderstood
I misunderstand the deadline yesterday.
I misunderstood the deadline yesterday.
Misunderstand becomes misunderstood in the past. Explain what happened and what you did next. Center is the American spelling.
Describe your technical leadership
Tell me about your role on Project Orion. I led a small software team, helped review API designs, and turned broad goals into weekly plans.
The speaker combined team leadership and API design reviews.
I ___ a small software team.
led
I lead a small team last year.
I led a small team last year.
Lead becomes led in the past. Describe specific actions instead of only a job title; a tech lead combines technical judgment with team coordination.
Explain an architecture trade-off
Tell me about a difficult decision. An integration was late, so I proposed keeping one service for the first release instead of adding three microservices. We could split it later if needed.
The speaker proposed one service to reduce initial scope.
I ___ keeping one service for the first release.
proposed
I propose a smaller release last month.
I proposed a smaller release last month.
Use past simple for a completed decision. Explain the constraint and trade-off; microservices are not automatically the best choice for every system.
Explain a delivery result
What was the result? We delivered the core API on time. As a result, the test team could validate the integration that week, and we used their feedback in the next release.
The delivery let the test team validate the integration that week.
We delivered on time. ___, testing could start.
As a result
We delivered on time, so testing could started.
We delivered on time, so testing could start.
As a result introduces an outcome; because introduces its cause. Describe an observable result without claiming unsupported business impact. After could, use start, not started.
Ask for feedback as a manager
How do you support the engineers on your team? I ask what is getting in their way, agree on priorities, and follow up on the actions we choose together.
The manager asks about obstacles and follows up on actions.
I ___ up on the actions we agree on.
follow
She follow up on the agreed actions.
She follows up on the agreed actions.
Follow up on an action means check its progress later. Add -s with she. An engineering manager supports the team by clarifying priorities and removing obstacles, not just requesting reports.
Ask about a new community activity
Do you have any questions about the class? Yes. What should I bring to the first session, and how long does it last?
The speaker asks what to bring and how long the class lasts.
How long ___ the class last?
does
How long does the class lasts?
How long does the class last?
Use does + subject + base verb. Asking what to bring and how long something lasts helps you join everyday activities with confidence.
Give an incident recovery update
What is the latest update on the incident? We restored the service yesterday. Today we are checking the logs. If the checks pass, we will close the incident tomorrow and schedule a follow-up review.
The service is restored, but checks are still in progress.
If the checks ___, we will close the incident.
pass
If the checks will pass, we will close the incident.
If the checks pass, we will close the incident.
Use present simple after if and will in the result. Restored service does not mean every follow-up action is complete; distinguish recovery from incident closure.
Compare architecture options

Why choose one service for now? It costs less to operate and is easier for our small team to maintain. Although microservices could help us scale parts separately later, we do not need that complexity yet.
One service fits the current team's needs with less complexity.
The smaller design is easier ___ maintain.
to
Although it is simpler, but it meets our needs.
Although it is simpler, it meets our needs.
Use easier to + verb. Do not combine although and but in the same construction. Compare current needs and operational cost instead of treating one architecture as universally best.
Clarify a contract dependency
What do you mean by a dependency here? We cannot finish the integration tests until the other team confirms the API response format. That decision is now blocking this step.
The unconfirmed response format is blocking the integration tests.
We cannot finish ___ the format is confirmed.
until
We cannot finish until the format will be confirmed.
We cannot finish until the format is confirmed.
Use present simple after until for a future condition. A dependency becomes a blocker when its missing result prevents the next step; describe that impact explicitly.
Lead a technical decision
Which option should we choose? First, compare the API compatibility risks. Next, choose the smaller change that meets the need. Finally, confirm the owner, test plan, and deployment date together.
The team should compare compatibility risks before selecting a change.
First compare the risks. ___, choose a change.
Next
First choose the date, finally compare risks, next name the owner.
First compare risks, next choose a change, finally confirm the owner.

Use sequence words to guide a decision. A software architect compares trade-offs, a tech lead coordinates the implementation, and an engineering manager helps align priorities; responsibilities can overlap.
Reflect on everyday fluency
What will you keep practicing? I will practice asking follow-up questions and telling short stories about my day. I can explain my plans more clearly now.
The speaker will practice questions and everyday stories.
I will keep ___ short stories.
telling
I will keep tell short stories.
I will keep telling short stories.
Keep takes an -ing form: keep telling. Reflect on what you can do and what to practice next without claiming a guaranteed language level.

The documentation is complete but no code exists.
Both the code and documentation are finished.

They plan to meet for coffee today.

The service is working normally and there is no incident.
The meeting time has not been agreed on.
The deployment review is at two tomorrow.
The pictures are already printed.
The album needs another month before printing.
They will hike regardless of the weather.
They have already canceled the hike.
The team has already decided to split the service.

The mobile team owns the response format.
The review is scheduled for ten.

Both the response and documentation must be removed.

The error rate has already increased after deployment.
They agreed to meet at a restaurant on Friday.
They decided that nobody should bring lunch.
The sample response is needed next week.
The integration test is already finished.
A late change requires no extra test work.
A late change adds two weeks of work.
Access was granted before the team requested it.
Testing already started on Monday with full access.
The chart should be finished before sign-in works.
Both tasks stop users from signing in.
The bus is both faster and more expensive.
They can wait until tomorrow to choose.
The reviewer should ignore existing clients.
The review is due next Monday.
Only risks need owners, and current issues should be omitted.
The report should remove all dates.
The service is already down today.
The team guarantees that traffic will not change.
The team wants to deploy to everyone without checks.
The team will discard the previous version before testing.
They have no plans for tomorrow.
They want to host a noisy party before the trip.
The deployment is already complete.
The team needs two more weeks to write the code.
Friday is impossible even with fewer features.
The optional export feature is required for Friday.
The speaker wants to remove integration testing.
The speaker sees no benefit in the proposed date.
All features will be delivered on Friday.
The team will decide who owns the work after next Tuesday.
The speaker registered for the original class on time.
The community center refused to discuss any other class.
The speaker only organized social events.

translations: ¿Qué haces en Project Orion? Coordino el equipo de software.
¿Quién revisa los resultados de las pruebas? La persona que lidera técnicamente al equipo los revisa cada viernes.
¿La ingeniera participa en la reunión del equipo? Sí, participa cada lunes.
¿Qué necesitan para preparar la cena? Primero necesitamos comprar arroz.
¿Eres nuestra nueva vecina? Sí. Vivo aquí con mi hermana.
¿Con qué frecuencia ejecutas las pruebas? Las ejecuto cada mañana antes de la reunión del equipo.
¿En qué estás trabajando esta semana? Estoy creando una API que permite a nuestra aplicación compartir datos.
¿Normalmente revisas código por la mañana? Sí, pero hoy estoy revisando un error de la aplicación.
¿Tu hermano está preparando la cena? Todavía no. Está comprando verduras en la tienda.
¿Qué necesita tu familia hoy? Una lista de compras, y la estamos escribiendo juntos.
¿Qué terminaste ayer? Arreglé el error de inicio de sesión antes del almuerzo y envié los resultados de las pruebas.
¿Aprobaron el diseño de la API? No, pidieron un ejemplo más claro de la respuesta.
¿Dónde está el informe de estado que comentamos? En la carpeta compartida, con las fechas y los problemas pendientes.
¿En qué estás trabajando en casa? En un álbum de fotos, pero estoy esperando más fotos.
¿Cómo estuvo tu visita al parque? Encontramos un lugar tranquilo, almorzamos y caminamos alrededor del lago.
¿Por qué se retrasó el despliegue? Falló una prueba, así que la estamos corrigiendo antes de desplegar la aplicación.
¿El servicio está listo? El código sí, pero la documentación de la API todavía necesita un ejemplo.
¿Cómo debo dar mi avance semanal? Primero di qué terminaste. Después menciona los impedimentos. Finalmente explica el siguiente paso.
¿Podrías repetirlo? ¿Nos vemos para tomar café hoy o mañana? Mañana, por favor.
Déjame aclararlo. La cena es en mi casa el sábado, no en el restaurante.
¿Cuál es tu avance semanal? Ayer terminamos las pruebas de la API. Hoy estamos revisando la integración y mañana compartiremos los resultados.
¿Qué impide hacer las pruebas? No podemos acceder al entorno de pruebas porque nuestra cuenta todavía no tiene permiso.
¿De qué depende la integración? Del contrato de la API, que el otro equipo confirmará el jueves.
¿Qué sigue? Necesitamos recoger las compras antes de preparar la cena.
¿Sigues trabajando en la bicicleta averiada? Sí, estoy tratando de arreglarla antes del viernes.
¿Qué van a probar la próxima semana? Dos microservicios juntos antes de cambiar la aplicación.
¿Quién puede revisar los registros mientras restablecemos el servicio? Yo los revisaré. Por favor mantén actualizado el canal del incidente.
¿Cuándo te reunirás con la arquitecta? Mañana a las diez para revisar el plan de despliegue. Ya está en el calendario.
¿Cuándo puedes terminar el álbum? Para el viernes, pero imprimir las fotos tomará otro día.
¿Iremos de excursión el sábado? Si está despejado, sí. De lo contrario, nos quedaremos en casa.
¿Qué tratamos primero? Confirmemos el problema que debemos resolver. Después podemos comparar mantener un servicio con dividirlo en dos.
¿Quién es responsable del formato de respuesta de la API? El equipo de plataforma, y la arquitecta revisará el cambio propuesto a las dos.
No estoy seguro de haber entendido. ¿Pides cambiar la respuesta de la API o solo su documentación? Solo la documentación; la respuesta sigue igual.
Perdón por interrumpir. Antes de desplegar, ¿podemos confirmar quién revertirá el cambio si aumenta la tasa de errores?
¿Qué acordamos? Reunirnos en el parque el miércoles y llevar almuerzo para compartir.
¿Qué necesitan de nosotros? Un ejemplo de respuesta de la API para el mediodía, para terminar hoy la prueba de integración.
¿Qué pasa si el contrato de la API cambia tarde? Necesitaremos dos días más para actualizar las pruebas de integración antes del despliegue.
¿Por qué estás escalando el problema de acceso? Lo pedimos el lunes y aún no hay decisión. Las pruebas están programadas para empezar mañana.
¿Qué problema corregimos primero? La falla de inicio de sesión, porque impide entrar a la aplicación. La gráfica opcional puede esperar.
¿Tomamos el autobús o vamos en auto? El autobús cuesta menos; sin embargo, ir en auto es más rápido. Debemos decidir antes de las seis.
¿Podrías revisar el cambio de la API para el jueves y señalar problemas de compatibilidad? Sí, enviaré comentarios antes del almuerzo.
¿Qué cambio en el informe de estado? Conserva el resumen de avances, pero agrega responsable y fecha objetivo para cada problema pendiente. Menciona como riesgos los posibles retrasos.
¿Está confirmada la lentitud del servicio? No. El tráfico podría aumentar la próxima semana, así que existe riesgo de respuestas más lentas. Hoy el servicio funciona normalmente.
¿Cómo reducimos el riesgo del despliegue? Despleguemos primero a un grupo pequeño de prueba, observemos la tasa de errores y tengamos listo un plan de reversión.
¿Por qué no invitar a todos esta noche? Me gustaría ver a nuestros amigos. Por otro lado, necesitamos una noche tranquila antes del viaje de mañana.
¿Pueden desplegar mañana? Podemos terminar el código mañana, pero necesitamos dos días más para las pruebas de integración. ¿Podemos desplegar el viernes?
¿Sigue siendo posible el viernes? Sí, si dejamos fuera la función opcional de exportación. Podemos entregar la API principal el viernes y agregar exportaciones en la próxima versión.
¿Estás de acuerdo con la fecha propuesta? Veo el beneficio, pero me preocupa el tiempo de pruebas. ¿Podemos conservar un día más para revisar la integración?
¿Cuál es el acuerdo final? Entregaremos la API principal el viernes. La exportación opcional llegará el próximo martes y la persona que lidera técnicamente confirmará hoy a los responsables.
¿Por qué se te pasó la fecha de inscripción? Entendí mal la fecha límite. Llamé al centro comunitario y me ayudaron a encontrar otra clase.
Háblame de tu función en Project Orion. Lideré un equipo pequeño de software, ayudé a revisar diseños de API y convertí metas generales en planes semanales.

Háblame de una decisión difícil. Una integración se retrasó, así que propuse mantener un servicio en la primera versión en vez de agregar tres microservicios. Podríamos dividirlo después si hiciera falta.
¿Cuál fue el resultado? Entregamos la API principal a tiempo. Gracias a eso, el equipo de pruebas validó la integración esa semana y usamos sus comentarios en la siguiente versión.
¿Cómo apoyas a las personas de ingeniería de tu equipo? Pregunto qué les dificulta avanzar, acordamos prioridades y doy seguimiento a las acciones que elegimos juntos.
¿Tienes preguntas sobre la clase? Sí. ¿Qué debo llevar a la primera sesión y cuánto dura?

¿Cuál es la última actualización del incidente? Restablecimos el servicio ayer. Hoy revisamos los registros. Si las comprobaciones salen bien, cerraremos el incidente mañana y programaremos una revisión posterior.

¿Por qué elegir un servicio por ahora? Cuesta menos operarlo y es más fácil de mantener para nuestro equipo pequeño. Aunque los microservicios podrían permitirnos escalar partes por separado después, aún no necesitamos esa complejidad.
¿Qué significa dependencia aquí? No podemos terminar las pruebas de integración hasta que el otro equipo confirme el formato de respuesta de la API. Esa decisión está impidiendo completar este paso.

¿Qué opción elegimos? Primero comparemos los riesgos de compatibilidad de la API. Después elijamos el cambio menor que cubra la necesidad. Finalmente confirmemos juntos responsable, plan de pruebas y fecha de despliegue.
¿Qué seguirás practicando? Haré preguntas de seguimiento y contaré historias breves sobre mi día. Ahora puedo explicar mis planes con más claridad.
